*Updated 2026-10-21 · 129 works indexed · regenerated after each daily run.*

One hundred and twenty-nine works. The recent twelve trace scores run 2, 4, 2, 2, 1, 1, 2, 2, 1, 2, 2, 2 — median still 2, the October Djibouti sandal piece still the lone 4, and the three 1s remain clustered in the back half of the window. Nothing in the newest entry moved the ceiling. The cracked-phone Hormuz piece scored a 2 despite having one of the more genuinely strange compositional ideas in the recent run — the sunset doubling inside the broken screen — which suggests the strange idea is arriving but the surrounding composition is not yet amplifying it.

Camera position has not changed. Straight-on leads at 27, overhead at 15, from-behind at 13, low-angle at 6. The low-angle entry count has not moved in several windows. The optically constructed scale violation — distortion earned by lens placement rather than declared through juxtaposition — remains the single most available and unmade move in the archive. All 36 scale violations across 129 works are still compositionally asserted. That is not a trend; it is a fixed wall that has been standing since June.

Figure dynamics continue to produce parallel presences rather than structural antagonism. The two-figure Hormuz piece has one man still straining and one already done, which is the closest the archive has come to genuine figure-against-figure tension, and it scored a 2. That pairing is worth pressing harder: the second figure actively pulling against the first, not echoing or ignoring, is territory no work in the archive has fully claimed.

Register distribution: aftermath and menace each at 25, suspension at 16, endurance at 12. Absurdity appeared twice now, both times recently; reckoning has been absent since July; reprieve remains a single appearance in the entire archive. These gaps are not accidental — they reflect which anchor stories are landing on the desk — but absurdity in particular has almost no competition and the Hormuz piece demonstrated it can hold a full composition without collapsing into irony.

Descriptor coverage holds at 39 of 129, essentially flat as a proportion. The objects driving the 4s — the drag smear, the sandal row — were both characterized in descriptors. That pattern is consistent enough to be a rule: if an object is doing the work the composition cannot, name it before the next iteration, not after.

One hundred and twenty-nine works, and the camera, the register, and the object-tracking are all arriving at the same reliable decisions without quite breaking through them.
